brief:
PROD-2451 — Add cursor-based pagination to GET /api/items

Our public API currently returns the full item list on every call. As we cross 1k items per merchant, the payload is too big and clients are timing out. Add cursor-based pagination to the existing handler:

- Accept `?limit=N&cursor=...` query params (default limit 20, max 100).
- Return `{ items: [...], next_cursor: string|null }`.
- A cursor encodes the last item's id so the next page is items after that id (lexicographic on the `_id` field).
- Preserve existing behaviour when no params are passed (still return up to 20 items + a cursor).

The codebase uses Express + an in-memory ItemStore module. Don't touch the storage layer; just extend the route handler.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/items returns at most `limit` items (default 20, capped at 100)
Response includes a `next_cursor` field; null when the page is the last one
GET /api/items?cursor=<value-from-prior-response> returns the page that follows
Invalid limit (negative, non-numeric, > 100) returns 400 with `{ error: 'invalid_limit' }`
Invalid cursor (not present in the store) returns 400 with `{ error: 'invalid_cursor' }`

hidden_tests.name: limit and cursor

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Compass may suggest `startIdx = idx` (off-by-one) which returns the cursor item again on the next page.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: The cursor 'points to' the last returned item; an inexperienced model returns slice.start = cursor index instead of cursor index + 1.
detection_signals: hidden test 'cursor advances the page' fails (page B contains page A's last id)

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Compass may forget to cap limit at 100, letting a client request 10000 items in one go.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Common pattern is to default missing values; the cap is the easier check to skip.
detection_signals: hidden test 'invalid limit returns 400' fails when limit=999

rubric_anchors.check: Learner runs tests at least twice and after each change
Cursor parsing is centralised, not duplicated; constants named

good_prompts_look_like: Ask for cursor semantics (does cursor point at the last returned item or the next one?)
Ask about behaviour when cursor is invalid
Ask about default vs maximum limit
common_verification_traps: Forgetting to run the test that exercises 'limit > MAX' rejection
decomposition_reference: Locate cursor index in the store

interview_parallel: Razorpay backend lateral round — paginated list endpoints come up in nearly every backend take-home.
